newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav business climate seen slightly worsening.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav business climate seen slightly worsening.

text.p: The business climate in Yugoslavia slightly deteriorated in November, the Economics Institute said in its latest monthly report on Wednesday.

Economists cited growing inflationary expectations, lack of working capital, a slowdown in industrial output growth and rising pessimism concerning future economic performance as key trends in November.

Presenting the report to journalists, Goran Pitic of the Belgrade-based think-tank said inflationary expectations signalled that the taming of inflationary forces needed to become a top priority of 1997 economic policy.
The latest survey of 300 companies showed optimism declining. Only 14.2 percent considered the current economic situation good, while 26.5 percent said it was bad.
At the same time, 6.7 percent of all companies found the business risks falling slightly, but 34.3 percent said it was increasing.
Some 34.2 percent of firms planned to increase output over next three months, while 10 percent expected a decline.
Almost a third of those surveyed expected prices of final products to rise over the next three months, and 58.6 percent saw raw-material prices surging.

The survey revealed growing concern about expected domestic sales and exports, with 40.9 percent of all companies expecting domestic sales to pick up, but 43.2 percent planning no exports over the next three months.
More than 13 percent of those surveyed said they had sufficient inventories of final products, but 40.8 percent said inventories were low.
Only 1.8 percent had high raw-material inventories but 55.4 percent said they were low.
